dataset.name: Boat-Dragged Riverbed and Mid-Column Water Quality along the Hanford Reach in the Columbia River Shorelines
description: This dataset contains water quality measurements used to identify sites of hydrologic exchange (i.e.hydrologic exchange flows; HEFs) in the Columbia River near Richland, WA by looking for anomalies in temperature and electrical conductivity (EC) along the bed of the river in February, June, July, August, and November 2017. These are ultimately the ‘ends’ of HEFs as they are locations of subsurface inflow to the river. This dataset contains dissolved oxygen (DO) measurements at 1-min intervals; temperature, EC, depth, and GPS coordinates at 1-second intervals; and N-NO3 at 2-min intervals along the river bed and mid-column water. DO measurements are included in this dataset for completeness but were not used in the analysis of HEFs due to the relatively long time interval of collection.

measurementTechnique: To compare the temperature and electrical conductivity (EC) along the riverbed with the water column, sensors were deployed on two ropes – one to measure along the riverbed, and the another approximately 1-2 m above the riverbed, depending on the depth of the water column. Several metal fishing weights were affixed to the end of each rope, and sensors were affixed approximately 0.3 meters from the end of the rope to prevent the weights from collision ding with the weights sensors and to allow the sensors to skim over the rocks on the riverbed, avoiding sensor damage. We used Campbell Scientific sensors: high-sensitivity T109 temperature probes (one in the shallow water column, one dragged along the bed), CS547 EC probes (one in the shallow water column, one dragged along the bed), and a GPS receiver. All of these sensors were connected to and controlled by a CR1000 datalogger, collecting at a one-second interval. A Submersible Ultraviolet Nitrate Analyzer (SUNA) Seabird sensor was used to measure nitrate concentrations from August 8-16, 2018. The SUNA sensor collected 15 readings at 2-second intervals, every two minutes from the shallow water column (it was not dragged along the bed). To verify the SUNA measurements, 10 grab samples of river water were collected adjacent to the SUNA unit on August 15. These samples were analyzed at PNNL using Fourier Transform Ion Cyclotron Resonance (FT-ICR) analysis, to measure for nitrate concentrations using in the grab samples a Dionex ICS-2000 anion chromatograph with AS40 auto sampler using an isocratic method. The nitrate concentration of grab samples ranged from 0 to 4.5 mg N-NO3/L. Lab measurements confirmed SUNA measurements within 5% difference.
